name: Observation of Single Isolated Electrons of High Transverse Momentum in Events with Missing Transverse Energy at the CERN anti-p p Collider

published.note: Year only; exact publication day not sourced in this session.

summary.plain: UA2 found four events with an isolated high-transverse-momentum electron and large missing transverse energy; the paper says their configuration and number are consistent with a W boson decaying into an electron and a neutrino. CERN's account has UA2's four candidate events presented to a packed CERN auditorium, a day or two after UA1's six.
summary.technical: UA2 Collaboration, Phys. Lett. B 122 (1983) 476-485: four candidate events with a single isolated high-p_T electron and missing transverse energy, consistent with p-pbar -> W(+/-) + anything, W -> e + nu. The result was presented by Luigi Di Lella at a CERN seminar (22 January 1983 per CERN's UA2 page; 'the following afternoon' after UA1's 20 January seminar per CERN's 2013 article), before the CERN announcement of the W discovery on 25 January 1983.

title: Observation of Single Isolated Electrons of High Transverse Momentum in Events with Missing Transverse Energy at the CERN anti-p p Collider
why_it_matters: A second experiment at the CERN proton-antiproton collider reporting events consistent with W production: four candidate events in UA2, alongside UA1's six.
